message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals, but they belong to different orders—Carnivora for lions and Perissodactyla for zebras. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade **Eutheria** (placental mammals), which lived roughly 160 million years ago during the Late Jurassic–Early Cretaceous. In other words, the common ancestor of lions and zebras was a small, shrew‑like mammal that gave rise to all modern placental mammals, from which the lineages that eventually produced carnivores and perissodactyls diverged.
